title: U.S. Senate · Michigan

context.text: Incumbent Democrat Gary Peters did not seek re-election, making this an open seat. Abdul El-Sayed won the Democratic primary and Mike Rogers ran unopposed for the Republican nomination in the August 4, 2026 primary.
Cook Political Report and Inside Elections rated the general election a Toss-up as of September 2026; Decision Desk rated it Lean Democratic.

candidates.name: Abdul El-Sayed
candidates.currentRole: Physician and epidemiologist; former director and health officer, Wayne County Department of Health, Human and Veterans Services (2022–2025)

summary.text: El-Sayed is a physician and epidemiologist who ran the Detroit Health Department after the city's bankruptcy and later ran an unsuccessful 2018 campaign for Michigan governor. He was director and health officer for the Wayne County Department of Health, Human and Veterans Services from 2022 to 2025 before entering the Senate race.

background.text: Earned a B.S. in biology and political science from the University of Michigan (2007), a D.Phil. in public health from the University of Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar (2011), and an M.D. from Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons (2014).
Hired in 2015 to lead Detroit's newly privatized health department after the city's bankruptcy; served until February 2017, when he left to run for governor.
Served as director and health officer for the Wayne County Department of Health, Human and Veterans Services from 2022 to 2025.

priorities.text: Enacting Medicare for All and eliminating medical debt nationwide.

positions.quote: I literally wrote the book on Medicare for All because healthcare is a human right, not a privilege. ... I will sponsor legislation to enact M4A and eliminate medical debt nationwide. M4A guarantees comprehensive coverage, eliminates co-pays and deductibles, and lowers overall costs through reducing administrative waste and negotiating drug prices.

positions.summary: Says he supports targeted tariffs on growth industries that sunset over time, and criticizes the current tariffs as making the problem worse.
positions.quote: I support targeted, smart tariffs that would help protect Michigan manufacturing and incubate the industries of the future with unions at the forefront.

positions.summary: Supports raising the marginal rate on earnings over $1 million, taxing capital gains over $1 million as ordinary income, and a tax on wealth over $1 billion.
positions.quote: I support raising the marginal tax rate on earnings over $1 million and a billionaire tax on wealth over $1 billion.

positions.summary: Described by Bridge Michigan as a vocal supporter of ending offensive U.S. military aid to the Israeli government.

candidates.name: Mike Rogers
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed for the Republican nomination

summary.text: Rogers represented Michigan's 8th Congressional District in the U.S. House from 2001 to 2015 and served in the Michigan Senate from 1995 to 2000. Before politics he served in the U.S. Army and worked as an FBI special agent; after leaving Congress he worked in cybersecurity and business.

background.text: Born in 1963 in Livingston County, Michigan; graduated Howell High School and Adrian College (B.S., 1985).
Served in the U.S. Army from 1985 to 1989, then worked as a special agent in the FBI.
Served in the Michigan Senate representing District 26 from 1995 to 2000, then represented Michigan's 8th Congressional District in the U.S. House from 2001 to 2015.
After leaving Congress, owned a business and worked as a cybersecurity professional.

priorities.text: Bringing manufacturing jobs back to the U.S. and lowering the cost of gas, groceries, and prescription drugs.
Protecting Social Security and Medicare for seniors.

positions.summary: Says tariffs are necessary to protect Michigan manufacturing but are not a one-size-fits-all solution.
positions.quote: President Trump is right to put America First - and tariffs are necessary, but are not a one-size-fits-all solution.

positions.summary: Bridge Michigan reports he opposed extending the enhanced premium tax credits for plans bought through HealthCare.gov.

candidates.researchNotes: Rogers's campaign site (mikerogers.com) is JavaScript-rendered and its issue pages (healthcare plan, housing plan) did not return readable text via direct fetch, so specific issue positions beyond the quoted priority statement in Ballotpedia's race summary could not be documented from primary sources within the time available.
